 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Another titan of this Scotland team is hunting down a record of his own.
 John McGinn is only eight caps behind team-mate Andy Robertson and Kenny Dalglish, but is now just six goals off the record shared by Dalglish and Denis Law.
 Four of Scotland's last six goals have been scored by the Aston Villa captain, making this year his for the national team since netting seven in 2019.

 The task facing Scotland published at 19:25 GMT 19:25 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Scotland have won just one of their last 11 games against sides ranked in the top 15 of the world rankings. Switzerland are currently 12th.
 The Swiss lead Nations League Group B1 by five points from Slovenia and have already secured promotion.
 Unbeaten in five games, their run of four straight wins ended with Friday's 0-0 draw in Slovenia. They have, however, won their latest five home competitive games.
 In this season's Nations League, they have faced the fewest shots (25) and shots on target (five) while also having the best expected goals against (1.18).
 4 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What happened on Friday? published at 19:22 GMT 19:22 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Scotland made hard work of it.
 After a fairly uneventful first half, Sebastien Pocognoli's side took the lead through a bit of direct play when John McGinn netted. That was quickly wiped out from a North Macedonia corner, though.
 Super John then added to his and his team's tally with a penalty, sealing an underwhelming win as Pocogonoli's men try to get to grips with a new system and style.
 Tonight's match marks the acid test of this group, hence why some fans are fearing the worst as the Scots struggle to convince.

 Permutations... published at 19:13 GMT 19:13 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 So Scotland still have the chance to finish second in Group B1 should they beat Switzerland, but they would also need Slovenia to fail to win away to North Macedonia. 
 Unlikely on both counts, we know. 
 Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle. The Swiss have already sealed that in this section.
 Meanwhile, teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face either a third-placed or bottom-placed team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

 Tom English 
BBC Scotland's chief sports writer on Sportsound 
 I'm looking for a performance from Scotland. I'm looking for a different formation, something that works. 
 Whatever the formation is it needs to produce a coherent performance, and even though Switzerland are missing some big names they're still probably a better team than Scotland. 
 I have low expectations, but the one hope I have is that it's a performance that makes sense.

 Much-changed Switzerland missing key men published at 19:04 GMT 19:04 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Switzerland have named a much-changed team, perhaps unsurprising given they have already won the group.
 Head coach Murat Yakin is without four key players, with Inter defender Manuel Akanji, captain Granit Xhaka of Sunderland, Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi, and Nottingham Forest winger Dan Ndoye all out.
 Sion striker Winsley Boteli earns his fourth senior cap, while 23-year-old Young Boys midfielder Alvyn Sanches is handed his seventh.
 Despite Xhaka's absence, the Swiss midfield is strong - Remo Freuler of Olympiacos captains the side alongside AC Milan's Ardon Jashari.
 Leeds United centre-back Nico Elvedi has impressed since moving to the Premier League from Borussia Monchengladbach in the summer and scored at Hampden in September.
 Full-back Isaac Schmidt - now at Young Boys - had a less memorable spell at Elland Road in the 2024-25 season before being loaned to Werder Bremen.

 'We are really proud' - Pocognoli on Robertson feat published at 18:55 GMT 18:55 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 More from Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli on captain Andy Robertson's historic evening: "I just tell him that he has to enjoy it and after it's just a bonus for the future.
 "So he needs to enjoy, to play with freedom. 
 "He has a lot of experience, so I don't need to tell him, but again, we are really proud of what we are living together with him. 
 "And the best way to have a good feeling for him is to have a good game."

 Pocognoli explains team selection published at 18:52 GMT 18:52 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Scotland head coach Sebastien Pognoli tells BBC Scotland: "We want to see a different profile regarding the opponent we will face today. 
 "Che [Adams] did very well in the first game. He struggled a little bit with his calf yesterday morning, that's also one of the reasons, but Oli [McBurnie] also deserves the opportunity to play. 
 "The second change is Aaron Hickey, to have some stability on the right side because Switzerland is a good team on both sides.
 "And also the physical management for Ben [Gannon-Doak], that's also the reason.
 "We have a lot of good players on the bench, we try to make the best decision, but one of the reasons is the physical aspect with them.
 "I'm surprised the question comes before the game [on sticking with a back three].
 "We create many chances against Slovenia away, North Macedonia away and in the last game at home, we play front-footed, we created chances. 
 "We keep two times a clean sheet, nearly three in the last game. 
 We need to have some response against a strong opponent away from home, because if we want to be successful in the future we need to play against that type of team and I think we have the quality to try to make it difficult."
 Media caption, Pocognoli defends three-at-back formation

 Robertson to cap it all as he takes King Kenny's crown published at 18:49 GMT 18:49 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Amy Canavan 
BBC Sport Scotland in St Gallen 
 Andy Robertson is set to become the most capped men's Scotland international. History.
 Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he is set to surpass his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul has stood for 40 years.
 On moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.
 But, in St Gallen, the spotlight will shine brightly on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he goes solo at the summit.
 Read more: Robertson to cap it all as he takes King Kenny's crown 
 Media caption, Scotland captain Robertson on hero Dalglish

 Robertson starts as McBurnie & Hickey come in published at 18:45 GMT 18:45 GMT 
 Switzerland v Scotland (19:45) 
 Sebastien Pocognoli switches two of the Scotland side that started Friday's unconvincing win over North Macedonia.
 Oli McBurnie is handed a start, replacing Che Adams at centre-forward, while Aaron Hickey comes in for Ben Gannon-Doak at right-wing back.
 The big news, though... Andy Robertson starts on a historic night for the captain.
 When the first whistle is blown, the left-back will take the record for most caps gained by a Scotland men's player.
 Image source, SNS Image caption, Imminent history-maker Andy Robertson (left) and Oli McBurnie start for Scotland
